$comment: SONAR MODULE (pack: sonar) — targets bizapps-sonar (schema __mj_BizAppsSonar). DEFINITIONS ONLY: Sonar's FactorCompiler compiles factors to SQL and computes scores live, so we ship the model + version + bands + related entities + factors + weights and let Sonar recompute scores/contributions/history after install (never pre-compute score rows). Each factor is EXECUTABLE: Declarative, a supported aggregation (Count/Recency) over a related entity linked by SourceRelatedEntityID, RelationshipPath '[]' so the compiler auto-resolves the FK path to the People anchor (all single-hop). Recency windows come from Factor.DateField (the real business date column) + a Rolling TimeWindow — correct on seeded data regardless of __mj_CreatedAt. Weights are DIFFERENTIATED and Additive (WeightedSum) and are FRACTIONS OF ONE: Sonar renders ModelFactor.Weight as a percentage where 1.0 = 100%, so the per-factor weights must sum to 1.0 across the model. They previously shipped as integers 1-3 summing to 17, which the Sonar UI displayed as 200% and 300% weights (team ruling 2026-07-30: the max is 100%). Engagement = breadth + recency + depth of real participation; a declining member scores below an active one because the engine counts the member's actual rows. Slug 'morecheese-engagement'. Integration-grade: model owner is a platform-pack staff user, so INSTALL_ORDER puts sonar after platform.

model.name: Member Engagement Score
model.description: Composite engagement score for federation members — breadth, recency, and depth of participation across events, governance, learning, advocacy, surveys, certifications, and competitions. The retention early-warning dial, computed live by Sonar.

sonar.$bandNote: A band set spans the full 0-100 score scale, and this one does: 0-22-33-46-100, contiguous, gated by 'sonar: bands tile 0..100 with no gaps'. What is CALIBRATED (not arbitrary) is where the three interior edges fall, because the roster's composite is left-skewed — most members do little, a few do a lot — so the quartiles sit low and the Engaged band is deliberately the widest. Adding spend and tenure (each reaching ~100% of members) lifted the whole distribution: under the previous 0/10/20/35 edges 47% of the roster came out Engaged and only 8% At Risk, which is backwards for a retention model. LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-30 (a real FactorCompiler FullPopulation recompute on a from-scratch install, superseding the earlier offline approximation): over the 2,109 MEMBERS the edges give At Risk 35.5% / Watch 19.3% / Stable 26.5% / Engaged 18.7% — more at risk than engaged, the right direction for a retention model. Member quartiles came out Q1=15.5, Q2=30.7, Q3=42.4, so the shipped 22/33/46 sit a few points above the quartiles and deliberately widen At Risk. Observed member range 2.17-68.21 (nothing reaches the top of the Engaged band; MinMax is bounded by the real population, not by 100). CAVEAT, and it is not about the edges: the model anchors to MJ_BizApps_Common: People, so a recompute also scores the 949 NON-MEMBER prospects, and 100% of them land in At Risk (no membership, no spend, no tenure). That drags the whole-population split to 55.5% At Risk and is why Sonar's header reads '2,105 members at risk' when only 749 members are actually At Risk. ScoreModel.PopulationFilter cannot fix it — it is a Kendo filter over the ANCHOR's own fields, and Person carries no member/prospect discriminator (Status is 'Active' for all 3,058). Fixing it means re-anchoring to MoreCheese: Member Profiles (which would break the single-hop RelationshipPath '[]' auto-resolve every factor relies on) or an upstream PopulationFilter that supports a related-entity existence predicate.

bands.label: At Risk
bands.description: Disengaged — renewal is in doubt without intervention.

bands.label: Engaged
bands.description: Highly engaged — advocates and volunteers live here.

sonar.$factorNote: aggregation Count except the Recency factor (days since last event; HigherIsBetter=false). dateField = the leaf entity's business date column, paired with a Rolling window; factors without a window are all-time. Sonar's MinMax normalizes each factor over the member population; WeightedSum with the per-factor weights below.

factors.name: Event Participation
factors.description: Events the member registered for in the last 12 months.

factors.name: Certifications
factors.description: Certifications the member has pursued or earned.

factors.name: Learning Activity
factors.description: Courses the member enrolled in over the last 12 months.

factors.name: Advocacy Participation
factors.description: Advocacy actions the member took over the last 24 months.

factors.name: Competition Entries
factors.description: Cheese competition entries the member has submitted.

factors.name: Event Recency
factors.description: How recently the member last attended an event (sooner is better).

factors.name: Survey Participation
factors.description: Surveys the member responded to over the last 24 months.

factors.name: Member Spend
factors.description: Total billed value of everything the member has ordered in the trailing 24 months — dues, events, credentials, publications and merchandise.

factors.name: Membership Tenure
factors.description: How long the member has belonged to the federation. Recency of the join date, inverted — an older join means longer tenure and a stronger relationship.

sonar.$weightNote: SCALE: weights are fractions of one and sum to exactly 1.0000 (0.18 x2 + 0.12 x3 + 0.056 x5 = 0.36 + 0.36 + 0.28). Sonar shows Weight as a percent, so a weight above 1.0 renders as >100% and is wrong by construction; gate 'sonar: factor weights sum to 1.0' holds the line. The three TIERS below preserve the earlier 3:2:1 intent. Weight now follows COVERAGE. The model used to put its joint-heaviest weight on committee service, certifications and advocacy — each present for about 5% of members — so three of eight factors were zero for 95% of the roster and most score breakdowns were a row of empty bars. Spend reaches 99% of members and tenure 100%, and neither was represented at all. The niche signals still count, they no longer dominate.
